origin: Team Gtechniq's story begins in a small, unassuming garage in rural Oxfordshire. Founded in 2015 by lifelong motorsport enthusiasts, Ben Collins and Sarah Davies, the team initially focused on amateur club racing, primarily in modified production cars. Ben, a skilled mechanic with a passion for extracting every last ounce of performance, poured his evenings into meticulously prepping the team's aging BMW 325i. Sarah, a shrewd strategist with a background in engineering, managed the logistical and financial aspects, often securing sponsorships from local businesses and, most famously, a fruitful partnership with Gtechniq, a leading car care product manufacturer. Their early races were a rollercoaster of mechanical failures and unexpected triumphs, with the highlight being a surprise podium finish at the Castle Combe Autumn Classic in their second year.
philosophy: Team Gtechniq operates on the principle of continuous improvement and a relentless pursuit of perfection, even on a limited budget. They believe in maximizing the performance of their equipment through meticulous preparation, data analysis, and a collaborative team environment. Their car development is largely focused on incremental gains and reliability, favoring proven solutions over radical innovation. The team fosters a culture of camaraderie and mutual respect, where every member's contribution is valued.
achievements: Podium finish at the Castle Combe Autumn Classic (2017)
Multiple class wins in local club racing series (2016-2019)
Consistent top-ten finishes in regional endurance races
Development of a successful in-house data analysis system, providing a competitive edge

teamPrincipal.name: Sarah Davies
teamPrincipal.background: Sarah holds a degree in Mechanical Engineering and initially worked as a design engineer before transitioning to motorsport management. She is known for her calm demeanor, strategic thinking, and ability to motivate the team even under pressure.

keyFigures.name: Ben Collins
keyFigures.description: Ben is the heart and soul of Team Gtechniq's engineering efforts, possessing an uncanny ability to diagnose and resolve mechanical issues. He's a self-taught mechanic with an encyclopedic knowledge of automotive technology.

keyFigures.name: Emily Carter
keyFigures.description: Emily joined the team in 2018 after completing her motorsport engineering degree. She is responsible for analyzing race data and translating it into actionable insights for car setup and driver performance improvements.

headquarters: Team Gtechniq operates out of a modest workshop located on the outskirts of Oxford. The facilities are basic but functional, comprising of two bays, a small office area, and a storage room. They rely on local suppliers for specialized services like engine dyno testing and wind tunnel analysis.
fanBase: Team Gtechniq enjoys a small but loyal fanbase consisting of local motorsport enthusiasts and Gtechniq customers. They are known for their friendly atmosphere and willingness to engage with fans at race events, often sharing insights into their technical approach.
